proof_summary: The cases \(n=2,3\) are computed directly, while for \(n=4\) the congruence \(10^i\equiv1+9i\pmod{81}\), applied to a number and its reversal, forces any positive common multiple below nine digits to have digit sum divisible by \(81\); the digit bound then forces all nine digits to be \(9\), proving minimality. For \(n\ge5\), the palindrome \(68899199886\) handles \(5\le n\le12\), and for larger \(n\) concatenating this 11-digit block \(3^{n-12}\) times gives a smaller palindrome divisible by \(3^n\), since its geometric-series factor gains one factor of \(3\) at each tripling.
